Flow Analytics — Vanna, Charm & Put Skew

March 20, 2026
VANNA & CHARM EXPOSURE
Vanna (dDelta/dSigma): when implied vol changes, dealers mechanically re-hedge their delta. Positive net vanna exposure = vol compression creates systematic equity buying pressure. Negative net vanna = vol expansion creates systematic equity selling pressure. Charm (dDelta/dT per day): delta decays daily with time even if price does not move. Near OPEX this effect accelerates sharply and can distort intraday price action.
PUT/CALL OI RATIO BY STRIKE
Put/Call OI Ratio (this chart): open-interest-based ratio per strike. Strikes with OI ratio > 1.5 have heavy put accumulation relative to calls — typically defensive institutional hedging. Strikes near zero or NaN had insufficient call OI (< 10 contracts) and are suppressed. Note: the Put/Call Skew signal on the Signal Dashboard uses a separate GEX-weighted ratio (total put GEX / total call GEX), not this OI chart. The two metrics are related but not identical — OI ratio reflects positioning volume, GEX ratio reflects gamma exposure and dealer hedging pressure.
